brief: UBS sales desk frames year-end risk around three linked threads. A 0.30% core CPI print last week put a 50bp December hike on the table. UBS and the market still base-case consecutive 25bp hikes in December and January, but persistent inflation and accelerating growth raise the risk of a shift from a three-hike adjustment toward a sustained hiking cycle, which UBS calls meaningful against Middle East tensions and AI repricing. The AI trade has rotated from AI beta to AI alpha as the market questions capex against monetization, producing a good-versus-bad balance sheet trade that favors self-funded AI capex over capital-markets-dependent spenders. Jensen Huang's departure as Nvidia CEO adds funding uncertainty given his role arranging creative AI financing. Positioning is bearish but not short. Systematic and discretionary investors have de-risked and rotated defensively rather than go net short, leaving light positioning that creates asymmetric upside if Fed, funding and geopolitical fears do not materialize. Separately reported: Japan's Q3 GDP contracted on weak consumption despite AI-driven capex strength, Fed officials debate hike pace rather than direction, Huang is weighing a comeback amid board and White House lobbying, China's October activity data missed broadly, and BoE's Pill signals further tightening.
